Sumimi v0.4.1 — **containers see their own memory limit**.

**The bug.** The server read `/proc/meminfo` to learn how much memory the
machine has — and in a container, that is the **host's** memory, not the
container's. So a container limited to 512 MB, on a 7.7 GB host, would size its
engine at 256 MB and its admission gate at 40 000 requests a second, and the
OOM reaper would kill it.

**The fix.** The server now reads the **cgroup's** limit (cgroup v2's
`memory.max`, cgroup v1's `memory.limit_in_bytes`) and uses **the smaller of
the two**: the machine's memory and the limit this process may actually use.
A `--memory=512m` container now gets the minimum tier — a 128 MB engine and
20 000 requests a second — which is what the box can take.

The heartbeat reports both, so the numbers are checkable:
`machine.ramBytes` (the machine) and `machine.ramLimitBytes` (the limit).

**No configuration is needed.** A plain install on a plain machine is
unchanged; only a container sees anything different, and it sees the right
thing.

| Linux (x86-64) | `sumimi-v0.4.1-Linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |
| Linux (ARM64) | `sumimi-v0.4.1-Linux-aarch64.tar.gz` |
| Windows (x86-64) | `sumimi-v0.4.1-Windows-x86_64.zip` |
| Windows (ARM64) | `sumimi-v0.4.1-Windows-aarch64.zip` |

Unpack it and run it:

```bash
sumimi serve --dir ./sumimi --port 3000
```
